beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Parallel or perpendicular, a line through a point is fixed by its slope and that point.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which equation is the line through five, negative one that is parallel to y equals three x plus six?

do.text: Which equation is the line through $(5,-1)$ that is parallel to $y=3x+6$

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its step goes across one, up three. Rise over run: three over one is three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Parallel lines never meet. Slide a copy, step and all, without turning, to the point.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Same step, same slope: three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now write its equation in point-slope form. It needs one point on the line, x one, y one, and the slope, m: y minus y one equals m times x minus x one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here the point is five, negative one, and the slope is three. So the rise, y plus one, is three times the run, x minus five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply out, then subtract one: y equals three x minus sixteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which equation is the line through three, negative five that is perpendicular to y equals negative three x minus four?

do.text: Which equation is the line through $(3,-5)$ that is perpendicular to $y=-3x-4$

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its step goes across one, down three: slope negative three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Perpendicular means meeting at a right angle. Carry a copy to the point, then give it a quarter turn.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The step turned with it: now up one for every three across. The slope is one third.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A common slip writes negative one third. But the turned line rises, so its slope is positive.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Use point-slope form again, with the point three, negative five and the slope one third: y plus five is one third of x minus three.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply out, then subtract five: y equals one third x minus six, the perpendicular line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which equation describes the horizontal line through seven, two?

do.text: Which equation describes the horizontal line through $(7,2)$

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Horizontal means flat: every point on it has y equal to two. No rise, so its slope is zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which equation describes the vertical line through seven, two?

do.text: Which equation describes the vertical line through $(7,2)$

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Vertical means upright: every point on it has x equal to seven. There is no run to divide by, so the slope is undefined.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Flat and upright meet at a right angle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A slide keeps the step, so parallel lines share one slope.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A quarter turn trades rise and run and changes one sign.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Then the point places the line.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: flip the slope and change its sign.
